questions.stem: How does a loudspeaker produce a louder sound?

options.text: The frequency of the alternating current is increased
The amplitude of the alternating current is increased

questions.explanation: Increasing the amplitude (size) of the alternating current increases the force on the coil, which makes the cone vibrate with a larger amplitude, producing a louder sound. Changing the frequency would change the pitch, not the volume.

questions.stem: Why can a loudspeaker function as a microphone (and vice versa)?

options.text: They have identical components, and the motor effect and electromagnetic induction are reverse processes
They both use permanent magnets only
Sound waves can only be created by electricity

questions.explanation: Microphones and speakers have essentially the same components: a coil, a magnet, and a diaphragm/cone. A speaker uses the motor effect (current in, motion out) while a microphone uses electromagnetic induction (motion in, current out). These are reverse processes, so the same device can work both ways.
